clue.text: What retiring swains are incapable of making

definitions.text: What retiring swains are incapable of making

parts.words: What retiring swains are incapable of making
parts.note: retiring swains sounds like suitors walking away, but here retiring means bashful: shy young lovers cannot bring themselves to make romantic approaches

explanation.surface: A wry remark about timid young suitors who never manage to woo anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' tempts you to think of withdrawing or going to bed; it means shy, and what a shy suitor never makes is a romantic overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic overtures or passes made towards a sweetheart are called this.

clue.text: Runaway affairs?

parts.note: runaway affairs suggests eloping lovers, but read literally these are things down which water runs away

explanation.definitionFit: Pipes and gutters carry waste water off, so they are literally where water runs away.

clue.text: Beer is found in the passage

indicators.note: the word is is placed inside the drink, which is where it is found

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pint has been spotted lying in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway between rows of seats in a church or theatre is a passage.

clue.text: They're all hard cases in this family

definitions.text: They're all hard cases in this family

parts.words: They're all hard cases in this family
parts.note: hard cases suggests tough criminals in a gangland family, but it means creatures with hard shells, and family is the biological classification

explanation.surface: A family in which every member is a tough nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cases' and 'family' paint a crime clan; the family is a zoological grouping of shelled creatures like crabs and lobsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and shrimps belong to this group of shelled arthropods, protected by hard exoskeletons.

clue.text: Get out of a tight situation

definitions.text: Get out of a tight situation

parts.words: Get out of a tight situation
parts.note: a tight situation sounds like a predicament, but tight is slang for drunk, so getting out of it means losing one's intoxication

explanation.surface: Advice on escaping from a tricky predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like 'difficult'; it is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering from drunkenness and becoming clear-headed again is the meaning of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: &&&&&& - food for thought here

parts.note: six ampersands: the count of them, six, is VI in Roman numerals
each ampersand is the symbol for the word and, so together they read as a plural of that word

explanation.surface: A row of ampersands offered up as a puzzle to chew over.
explanation.walkthrough: Six ampersands make 'six ands'; six is VI in Roman numerals, giving VI + ANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for items of food, especially fine dishes and provisions.

clue.text: Sinuous slave dance

indicators.note: sinuous means winding and twisting, so the letters of the next word are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A serpentine dance performed by a slave.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a waltz, a ballroom dance in three time.

clue.text: Make sweet turnover to follow a spring vegetable

indicators.note: the reversed sweetening comes after the earlier pieces, following them in the answer

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: a turnover is a flipping, so the word for sweetening is turned back to front

parts.note: to sugar something is to make it sweet

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dessert: sweeten a pastry turnover to come after a seasonal vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like a pastry; it is the reversal signal, turning SUGAR into RAGUS after A and SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Green spears grown as a crop and eaten cooked, a popular early-summer vegetable.

clue.text: Do without and give to others

definitions.meaning: to hand out or distribute supplies to people

explanation.surface: Go without something yourself and pass it on to other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense comes from the phrase 'dispense with'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both doing away with something (with 'with') and distributing it, as a pharmacist does medicine.

clue.text: It's capital as a sun resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday advert praising a sunny resort as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like 'excellent' and 'resort' like a holiday destination; resort is re-sort, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Is it operated by the ring-finger?

definitions.text: Is it operated by the ring-finger?

parts.words: Is it operated by the ring-finger?
parts.note: ring-finger suggests the digit for a wedding ring, but here it is any finger that rings, pressing a button to sound a bell

explanation.surface: A question about what the fourth finger of the hand is used for.
explanation.definitionFit: A button pressed on a door frame to sound a bell indoors.

clue.text: A relatively historical figure

parts.note: relatively seems to mean comparatively, but it means as a relative: a family member from history

explanation.definitionFit: A forebear from whom one is descended is a relation from the past.

clue.text: Got out of doing something

parts.note: got out of doing something sounds like dodging a task, but it means obtained as a result of working

explanation.surface: Someone has wriggled out of a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got out of' suggests avoiding work; it means gained through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are gained in return for labour, so this verb means received as payment for work.

clue.text: Entertainer is to go places when free

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are set free to move into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer whose aim, once released, is to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'free' also describes the entertainer, whose act is breaking free from chains.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer like Houdini who wriggles out of locks, chains and straitjackets.

clue.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

definitions.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

parts.words: Return to the country, the scene of the crime
parts.note: sounds like a criminal revisiting the place of the offence, but it describes the legal handing over of a fugitive to the nation where they offended

explanation.surface: A guilty person goes back to the place where the crime happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the saying that criminals return to the scene of the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally surrendering a suspect to the state where the alleged offence took place.

clue.text: Omits the signs of spring

definitions.meaning: new foliage appearing on trees, read as leaves coming out

explanation.surface: Someone skips over the first indications that spring has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means excludes, and read literally describes foliage emerging in the season of growth.

clue.text: Court sadly lacks a seat for the lord chancellor

definitions.text: a seat for the lord chancellor

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: sadly suggests the next word is in a sorry state, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a law court has no chair for its senior judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court; it is the verb meaning woo. 'Sadly' rearranges LACKS to LSACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The wool-stuffed cushion in the House of Lords on which the presiding officer traditionally sits.

clue.text: Chap splits drinks with us — bags of them

indicators.note: the man splits apart the two drinks by sitting between them

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
tea is a hot drink
a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man divides beverages with us, and has lots of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' supplies two pieces, PORT and TEA, with MAN between them. 'Bags of them' looks like 'lots'; the definition is bags as luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Large travelling cases that open into two halves are a kind of luggage.

clue.text: Fit pet

definitions.meaning: a sudden outburst, as in a fit of rage
an old word for a sulk or fit of peevishness

explanation.definitionFit: An outburst of bad temper, like a child's screaming fit or a sulky huff.

clue.text: Outsize bloomer made by Egyptian god

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a bloomer is something that blooms, here the iris flower

explanation.surface: An enormous blunder committed by a deity of the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder (British slang) or bread; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient deity of the underworld and resurrection in the religion of the pharaohs.

clue.text: A lieutenant bearing one star

parts.note: LT is the military abbreviation for lieutenant
air means a person's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A junior officer wearing a single star on his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest point of light in the constellation Aquila is a celestial body of this name.

clue.text: Pay scales

parts.note: the phrase reads as a single idea, the amounts charged or paid per unit, such as hourly charges

explanation.definitionFit: Fixed charges or levels of payment, as in hourly wage levels.

clue.text: Unnecessary to curtail one's requirements

parts.note: the clue says it is not required to cut back, while split in two the word suggests needing less

explanation.surface: A claim that there is no point in cutting back on what one needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NEED LESS, the word describes curtailing one's requirements, while as one word it means unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superfluous or uncalled for is not required.

clue.text: Not so high clouds may threaten so

definitions.meaning: situated further down; comparative of a word for not tall
dark clouds frown or look menacing, the sense also spelt lour

explanation.surface: Clouds that hang lower look more menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning not tall, and also a verb for skies looking dark and menacing.

clue.text: Support at hand for those on flight

definitions.text: Support at hand for those on flight

parts.words: Support at hand for those on flight
parts.note: a flight sounds like an air journey, but it is a flight of stairs, and the support is a handrail that one grips

explanation.surface: Help is available for airline passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel; it is a staircase, and 'at hand' is literal: it is gripped by the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The handrail running beside a staircase is gripped for support while climbing.

clue.text: Going to the front, place of duty for nurse

definitions.meaning: a nurse working in a hospital room is on the ward

explanation.surface: A nurse heads off to the battlefront to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ON WARD, it says where a hospital nurse is on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means forwards or advancing, and read as two words gives a nurse's working position in a hospital.

clue.text: Balls hit high, right into the heavens

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for the heavens

parts.note: the skies are the heavens

explanation.surface: Cricket balls struck up high, straight into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skier is a ball hit very high into the air, usually an easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketing term for a mishit shot that goes steeply upwards.

clue.text: The smartest form of bedding

indicators.note: a different form of the word, so its letters are rearranged into new shape

explanation.surface: The most stylish kind of bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' could mean shape or type of bedding; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The padded base laid on a bed frame to sleep on is part of the bedding.
